episodes.request: An editor asks why the title "Don't Panic" becomes dont-panic and not don-t-panic. Where is that decided, and which apostrophes does it cover?

steps.thought: The slug is built in slugify.py; read it.
steps.output:
"""Turn a title into a URL slug. The rules are in docs/SLUG_RULES.md.

>>> slugify("Fish & Chips: Don't Panic!")
'fish-and-chips-dont-panic'
>>> slugify("A Very Long Title For A Page", max_length=14)
'a-very-long'
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from collections.abc import Iterable

from textkit.translit import fold

SEPARATORS = ("-", "_")
#: Symbols that are read as words (rule 3).
SYMBOL_WORDS = {"&": " and ", "@": " at "}
#: Characters that are removed without leaving a gap (rule 4).
APOSTROPHES = "'\u2019\u2018`"

_WORD = re.compile(r"[a-z0-9]+")


def _check_options(separator: str, max_length: int | None) -> None:
    if separator not in SEPARATORS:
        raise ValueError(f"separator must be '-' or '_', not {separator!r}")
    if max_length is not None and max_length < 1:
        raise ValueError(f"max_length must be at least 1, not {max_length}")


def _truncate(slug: str, separator: str, max_length: int) -> str:
    """Cut ``slug`` to at most ``max_length`` characters, after a whole word if possible."""
    if len(slug) <= max_length:
        return slug
    if slug[max_length] == separator:
        return slug[:max_length]
    head = slug[:max_length]
    boundary = head.rfind(separator)
    return head[:boundary] if boundary > 0 else head


def slugify(
    text: str,
    *,
    separator: str = "-",
    max_length: int | None = None,
    stopwords: Iterable[str] = (),
) -> str:
    """The slug for ``text``: lowercase ASCII words joined by ``separator``.

    Args:
        text: The title.
        separator: ``-`` (the default) or ``_``.
        max_length: Longest slug to return; a longer slug is cut after the last whole word
            that fits (or in the middle of the first word when it alone is too long).
        stopwords: Words to leave out, whatever their case. A title that consists of
            stopwords only keeps its words.

    Returns:
        The slug; empty when ``text`` has no letters or digits that survive folding.

    Raises:
        TypeError: ``text`` is not a string.
        ValueError: ``separator`` or ``max_length`` is not allowed.
    """
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise TypeError(f"text must be a string, not {type(text).__name__}")
    _check_options(separator, max_length)
    for symbol, word in SYMBOL_WORDS.items():
        text = text.replace(symbol, word)
    text = fold(text)
    for apostrophe in APOSTROPHES:
        text = text.replace(apostrophe, "")
    words = _WORD.findall(text.lower())
    skipped = {word.lower() for word in stopwords}
    kept = [word for word in words if word not in skipped]
    if kept:
        words = kept
    slug = separator.join(words)
    if max_length is not None:
        slug = _truncate(slug, separator, max_length)
    return slug

finish.thought: The loop in slugify removes the apostrophe characters before words are split.
finish.report: It is decided in slugify in src/textkit/slugify.py. The constant APOSTROPHES lists four characters: the straight apostrophe, the right and left single quotation marks (U+2019 and U+2018), and the backtick. After the title is folded to ASCII, slugify removes each of them with text.replace(apostrophe, ""), before the words are found with the pattern [a-z0-9]+, so Don't becomes Dont and then dont. Any other punctuation, such as a hyphen or a comma, is not removed that way: it ends a word and so becomes a separator.

episodes.request: When two pages have the same title, how does unique_slug choose the second slug, and what happens with max_length?

steps.thought: unique_slug lives in unique.py; read it.
steps.output:
"""Slugs that do not collide with the slugs already in use (rule 8 of docs/SLUG_RULES.md)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Collection

from textkit.slugify import slugify

#: The slug of a title that has no letters or digits.
FALLBACK_SLUG = "untitled"


def unique_slug(
    title: str,
    taken: Collection[str],
    *,
    separator: str = "-",
    max_length: int | None = None,
) -> str:
    """The slug of ``title``, numbered from 2 (``intro-2``, ``intro-3``) if it is in ``taken``.

    The number counts toward ``max_length``: the base slug is shortened to make room.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``separator`` or ``max_length`` is not allowed.
    """
    base = slugify(title, separator=separator, max_length=max_length) or FALLBACK_SLUG
    if max_length is not None:
        base = base[:max_length]
    if base not in taken:
        return base
    number = 2
    while True:
        suffix = f"{separator}{number}"
        stem = base
        if max_length is not None and len(stem) + len(suffix) > max_length:
            stem = base[: max(max_length - len(suffix), 1)].rstrip(separator)
        candidate = f"{stem}{suffix}"
        if candidate not in taken:
            return candidate
        number += 1

steps.output:
# textkit

Small text helpers for the publishing tools. Today that is URL slugs: `slugify` turns a
page title into the last part of its URL, and `unique_slug` makes sure that two pages do
not get the same one. The rules are written down in `docs/SLUG_RULES.md` (maintained by
the localization team).

## Library

    from textkit import slugify, unique_slug

    slugify("Fish & Chips: Don't Panic!")             # "fish-and-chips-dont-panic"
    slugify("Straße nach Köln", separator="_")        # "strasse_nach_koln"
    slugify("A Very Long Title", max_length=12)       # "a-very-long"
    slugify("The Rust Book", stopwords=["the"])       # "rust-book"
    unique_slug("Intro", {"intro", "intro-2"})        # "intro-3"

`slugify(text, *, separator="-", max_length=None, stopwords=())` raises `TypeError` for
a value that is not a string and `ValueError` for a separator other than `-` and `_` or
a `max_length` below 1. `unique_slug(title, taken, *, separator="-", max_length=None)`
takes the slugs that are in use.

## Command line

    $ python3 -m textkit slug "Hello, World!" "Ça va?"
    hello-world
    ca-va
    $ printf 'Intro\nIntro\n' | python3 -m textkit unique
    intro
    intro-2

`textkit slug TITLE...` prints one slug per title (`-` reads titles from standard
input, one per line) and takes `--separator`, `--max-length`, and `--stopwords a,b`.
`textkit unique` reads titles from standard input and numbers the repeated slugs. Errors
are printed to stderr as `textkit: error: ...` with exit status 2.

## Development

    python3 -m pytest -v

The package lives in `src/textkit/` and uses only the standard library.

finish.report: unique_slug in src/textkit/unique.py builds the base slug with slugify (using FALLBACK_SLUG, which is untitled, when the slug is empty) and returns it if it is not in taken. Otherwise it tries the separator and a number, starting at 2, until the candidate is free: intro, intro-2, intro-3, as the README example shows. With max_length, the number counts toward the limit: when the base plus the suffix would be too long, the base is shortened to max_length minus the length of the suffix (at least one character) and trailing separators are stripped before the suffix is added.

import io

from textkit.cli import main


def run(capsys, *args):
    status = main(list(args))
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    return status, captured.out, captured.err


def test_slug_prints_one_line_per_title(capsys):
    status, out, _ = run(capsys, "slug", "Hello World", "Second Page")
    assert (status, out) == (0, "hello-world\nsecond-page\n")


def test_slug_reads_titles_from_stdin(capsys, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", io.StringIO("First Page\nSecond Page\n"))
    status, out, _ = run(capsys, "slug", "-")
    assert (status, out) == (0, "first-page\nsecond-page\n")


def test_slug_takes_the_default_separator_explicitly(capsys):
    assert run(capsys, "slug", "--separator", "-", "Two Words")[1] == "two-words\n"


def test_an_unknown_separator_is_an_error(capsys):
    status, out, err = run(capsys, "slug", "--separator", "+", "Two Words")
    assert (status, out) == (2, "")
    assert err == "textkit: error: separator must be '-' or '_', not '+'\n"


def test_unique_prints_slugs_for_distinct_titles(capsys, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.stdin", io.StringIO("Overview\nInstall Guide\n"))
    status, out, _ = run(capsys, "unique")
    assert (status, out) == (0, "overview\ninstall-guide\n")
